title: Do Consumers Respond to Social Movements? Evidence from Gender-Stereotypical Purchases After #MeToo
eligible_reason: Single common event date: #MeToo onset (15 Oct 2017) is the same for all 32 countries (exposure.dta: metoo_week==1 starts 2017-10-15 in every country); after = metoo_week > 0. Treatment contrast is a triple difference (after x stereotypical product x exposed country), so there is one adoption cohort. Headline columns are ppmlhdfe (Poisson); the linear robustness columns (tab_altmodels.do) keep the same single-date DDD and add log price.
design_notes: Product x country x week panel of size stockouts and prices from a fashion retailer (StyleSage/Centric data), +/-6 weeks around 15 Oct 2017 (period_6w), women's shoes in 2017. Table (tab_main.do): ppmlhdfe stockout on after##feminine##treated, with lprice, absorb(product_ctry [country_month | country_week]), cluster country_id. treated = country above lowest tercile of #MeToo exposure (tweets/search/headlines index); feminine = stereotypical product marker. Robustness: other categories, time windows, seasonality (2018 placebo), alternative exposure measures, linear models (asinh, fraction, any stockout), clustering. Survey experiment and product-rating regressions are cross-sectional.

specs.exclusion_reason: single common event date (15 Oct 2017) for all countries; Poisson; triple interaction; time-varying lprice control
single common date; DDD with lprice control; robustness table

data_provenance_note: Readme.pdf: the product-level StyleSage/Centric Software data 'cannot be shared publicly'; raw_size_tracking.dta, raw_price_tracking.dta, raw_models.dta are not in the package. Shipped: exposure.dta (country-day exposure and metoo_week), survey_ratings.dta, survey_experiment.dta, and the full Stata log (Results/*.smcl).
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). Abstract describes a triple difference across time, countries and products around a single global movement date; no staggered element.
